Ssam with Ssamjang

Korean · Easy · Serves 4 (the modern ssam spread)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
**Lane: modern — the ssam bar, built around the pastes.** The ssam table's grammar (the leaf, the sauce, the meat, the fold) belongs to the grill site's tradition (#F01 there); this record is the modern spread — a gochujang-spiked ssamjang, quick seared fillings, and a build-your-own board that turns a weeknight into a ssam bar. The paste runs the whole board: the ssamjang's heat, a cho-gochujang dip for the vegetables, and a lacquered pan-seared pork that takes ten minutes. **Heat dial: 3, dropping to 2 if the table skews mild.**

Ssam with Ssamjang

Prep: 20 minutes · Cook: 10 minutes · Total: About 30 minutes · Serves 4 (the modern ssam spread)

Ingredients

The gochujang ssamjang

  • 3 tbsp doenjang (about 60 g)
  • 1.5 tbsp gochujang (about 30 g)
  • 1 tbsp honey (about 20 g)
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil (15 ml)
  • 2 cloves garlic (about 8 g), grated; half a small onion (about 40 g), grated
  • 1 tsp sesame seeds (about 4 g)

The cho-gochujang dip (the board's second bowl)

  • 2 tbsp gochujang (about 40 g)
  • 1.5 tbsp rice vinegar (about 22 ml)
  • 1 tbsp honey (about 20 g)
  • A splash of water (about 15 ml) and a pinch of gochugaru (about 1 g)

The quick fillings

  • 500 g pork shoulder or belly, sliced 5 mm, seared hot in a lightly oiled pan 2 minutes a side (or the weeknight shortcut: 300 g of good ham or tofu pressed and seared)
  • Steamed rice (about 500 g cooked), garlic coins (about 30 g), sliced chili (about 10 g)

The leaves

  • Lettuce cups and perilla (about 30 leaves), washed and bone-dry

Instructions

  1. The pork seared in batches at high heat, pulled to the board, and scissored into bite pieces. Checkpoint — browned edges, juicy centers, and the pan's fond left behind — deglaze it with a spoon of water and scrape the drippings into the ssamjang bowl (the old restaurant move: the sauce drinks the meat's flavor).
  2. The board: sauces at center, pork warm beside, leaves, rice, garlic, and chili in their quadrants. Checkpoint — every seat reaches all five — leaf, both sauces, pork, rice — without a pass. The board's geometry is the recipe's architecture.
  3. The build, the tradition's own sequence: leaf, a swipe of ssamjang (or the cho-gochujang for the sweet-heat fork), a piece of hot pork, a garlic coin, a pinch of rice, fold, one bite. Checkpoint — the eating test between the two sauces' bites: the ssamjang's fermented depth against the cho-gochujang's bright-sweet-heat — the same pork, two different sauces, two different ssams. That comparison is the board's whole evening.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Ssamjang flatMissing the fond or the honeyDeglaze into it; both are load-bearing
Cho-gochujang too thick to swipeUnder-loosenedWater by the splash; vinegar by the taste
Leaves tearing at the foldWet leaves or overfillingBone-dry; the fold is one bite's worth
Board assembled coldPan came before the boardBoard first, always — the sear is the last act

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- Both sauces keep a week refrigerated and improve; the board is a night's event. Seared pork keeps 3 days for the lunchbox ssam. - Variations: the #SF11-style seared tofu for the plant table; bulgogi slices (#M01's build) for the fuller board; a bowl of the kimchi (#2) as the board's third sauce in solid form.
